svg.title: Four Checks Before Purchase or Release
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-device-release-decision-tree; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Purchase or Release; subtitle: A failed check moves the lot into documented hold or rejection, never an automatic exception.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values indicate check order, not risk scores. Each affirmative branch advances to the next check; unresolved evidence holds the lot, and an unremediable defect rejects it. Complete purchase-stage checks before commitment and repeat release-stage checks before shipment. Requirements depend on device, activity, destination, and data role.; caption: Keep title, device regulation, patient-data handling, and biological safety as distinct evidence tracks. Passing one does not satisfy another.; stages: label: Clear title and transfer authority?; value: Yes: advance | Unresolved: hold purchase; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Match seller authority, asset serials, sale terms, and relevant lien searches. Under UCC 9-315, a security interest can survive a sale unless disposition is authorized or another rule applies. Obtain applicable release evidence; reject assets the seller cannot lawfully transfer.; label: Correct device and activity classification?; value: Yes: advance | Duty unresolved: hold work; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Review intended use, prescription restrictions under 21 CFR 801.109, and whether proposed work constitutes remanufacturing. Assess registration and listing under 21 CFR Part 807 and manufacturer quality-system duties under Part 820 when applicable. Check destination-state licensing and radiation requirements; do not assume every reseller must register as a manufacturer.; label: Patient-data exposure resolved?; value: Yes: advance | Verification fails: hold media; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Identify drives, removable media, network credentials, and embedded storage. Determine covered-entity or business-associate responsibilities under 45 CFR 164.502(e), with written terms under 164.504(e) where required. For regulated handling, apply 164.310(d) device and media controls; verify sanitization while preserving safe device operation and software entitlements.; label: Decontamination and functional acceptance complete?; value: Yes: release | Evidence incomplete: quarantine; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Require manufacturer-compatible decontamination records, calibrated biomed results, accessory completeness, recall resolution, and agreed buyer acceptance limits. Where occupational exposure is reasonably anticipated, apply 29 CFR 1910.1030 bloodborne-pathogen controls. Reject equipment lacking a credible route to safe, supported operation.

text.title: Four Checks Before Purchase or Release
text.tspan: Four Checks Before Purchase or Release

circle.title: label: Clear title and transfer authority?; value: Yes: advance | Unresolved: hold purchase; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Match seller authority, asset serials, sale terms, and relevant lien searches. Under UCC 9-315, a security interest can survive a sale unless disposition is authorized or another rule applies. Obtain applicable release evidence; reject assets the seller cannot lawfully transfer.

text.title: Match seller authority, asset serials, sale terms, and relevant lien searches. Under UCC 9-315, a security interest can survive a sale unless disposition is authorized or another rule applies. Obtain applicable release evidence; reject assets the seller cannot lawfully transfer.

circle.title: label: Correct device and activity classification?; value: Yes: advance | Duty unresolved: hold work; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Review intended use, prescription restrictions under 21 CFR 801.109, and whether proposed work constitutes remanufacturing. Assess registration and listing under 21 CFR Part 807 and manufacturer quality-system duties under Part 820 when applicable. Check destination-state licensing and radiation requirements; do not assume every reseller must register as a manufacturer.

text.title: Review intended use, prescription restrictions under 21 CFR 801.109, and whether proposed work constitutes remanufacturing. Assess registration and listing under 21 CFR Part 807 and manufacturer quality-system duties under Part 820 when applicable. Check destination-state licensing and radiation requirements; do not assume every reseller must register as a manufacturer.

circle.title: label: Patient-data exposure resolved?; value: Yes: advance | Verification fails: hold media; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Identify drives, removable media, network credentials, and embedded storage. Determine covered-entity or business-associate responsibilities under 45 CFR 164.502(e), with written terms under 164.504(e) where required. For regulated handling, apply 164.310(d) device and media controls; verify sanitization while preserving safe device operation and software entitlements.

text.title: Identify drives, removable media, network credentials, and embedded storage. Determine covered-entity or business-associate responsibilities under 45 CFR 164.502(e), with written terms under 164.504(e) where required. For regulated handling, apply 164.310(d) device and media controls; verify sanitization while preserving safe device operation and software entitlements.

circle.title: label: Decontamination and functional acceptance complete?; value: Yes: release | Evidence incomplete: quarantine; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Require manufacturer-compatible decontamination records, calibrated biomed results, accessory completeness, recall resolution, and agreed buyer acceptance limits. Where occupational exposure is reasonably anticipated, apply 29 CFR 1910.1030 bloodborne-pathogen controls. Reject equipment lacking a credible route to safe, supported operation.

text.title: Require manufacturer-compatible decontamination records, calibrated biomed results, accessory completeness, recall resolution, and agreed buyer acceptance limits. Where occupational exposure is reasonably anticipated, apply 29 CFR 1910.1030 bloodborne-pathogen controls. Reject equipment lacking a credible route to safe, supported operation.

Assumptions: Numeric values indicate check order, not risk scores. Each affirmative branch advances to the next check; unresolved evidence holds the lot, and an unremediable defect rejects it. Complete purchase-stage checks before commitment and repeat release-stage checks before shipment. Requirements depend on device, activity, destination, and data role.
